issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'תַּכְלִית שִׂנְאָה שְׂנֵאתִים' means 'I hate them with perfect hatred' (or 'I hate them with utmost hatred'), where 'תַּכְלִית' is an adverb/adjective meaning 'complete/utmost' modifying 'שִׂנְאָה' (hatred), and 'שְׂנֵאתִים' is the verb 'I hate them'. The Chinese rendering '恨惡的終結就是我所恨惡的' ('the end of hatred is what I hate') misinterprets 'תַּכְלִית' as 'end/termination' and changes the subject/object relationship, making it say something different from the Hebrew.
